scope: ŚB 3.19.1–3.19.38; 34 supplied Śrīdhara commentary blocks and four explicit न व्याख्यातम् markers.

entries.sanskrit:
ऊनविंशे विरिञ्च्यादि- प्रार्थितेन महा-मृधे ।

वराहेण हिरण्याक्ष- वधः श्लाघ्योऽनुवर्ण्यते ॥

निर्व्यलीकं च तद् अमृतं च । पाठान्तरे निष्कपटाभिप्रायं च तद् ऋतं च । कालात्मनोऽपि मम मुहूर्त-बलम् उपदिशतीति प्रहस्यापाङ्गालोकनेन स्वी-कृतवान् ॥१॥
word_for_word: requested by Brahmā and the others
“you teach me the power of a moment”
thus, smiling and glancing from the corner of his eye
entries.literal_english: In the nineteenth chapter, the praiseworthy slaying of Hiraṇyākṣa by Varāha in the great battle, requested by Brahmā and the others, is described. “Guileless” means sincere, and “nectarean” means dear. In an alternative reading, “guileless in intention” and “true” are the meanings. Although Brahmā speaks of the power of a moment even to the Lord who is Time personified, the Lord accepts his words with a smile and a sidelong glance.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.१ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.
transliteration:
ūnaviṃśe viriñcyādi- prārthitena mahā-mṛdhe |

varāheṇa hiraṇyākṣa- vadhaḥ ślāghyo’nuvarṇyate ||

nirvyalīkaṃ ca tad amṛtaṃ ca | pāṭhāntare niṣkapaṭābhiprāyaṃ ca tad ṛtaṃ ca | kālātmano’pi mama muhūrta-balam upadiśatīti prahasyāpāṅgālokanena svī-kṛtavān ||1||

entries.sanskrit: मुखतः अभिमुखे । हनौ कपोलस्याधो-भगे । अक्षजो ब्रह्मणो घ्राणेन्द्रियाद् आविर्भूतः ॥२॥
word_for_word: from Brahmā’s organ of smell, the nostril
entries.literal_english: “Mukhataḥ” means face-to-face, directly in front. “Hanau” means on the jaw, below the cheek. “Akṣajaḥ” means born from Brahmā’s organ of smell, that is, his nostril.

entries.sanskrit: सा स्व-गन्दया तेन हता ततो विहता विच्युत सती विघूर्णिता भूत्वापतद् रेजे च । तद् भगवत्-करात् पतनम् । यद् वा, तत् पदस्यावृत्त्या रेजे इत्य् अनेनापि संबन्धः तद् दैत्य-पौरुषं रेजे इति ॥३॥
word_for_word: that fall from the Lord’s hand
“shone” is connected in this way too
entries.literal_english: Struck by his own mace, it was knocked away; having fallen, it spun around and shone. This refers to its falling from the Lord’s hand. Alternatively, by repeating the word “that,” “shone” may be connected with the demon’s valor: his prowess shone.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.३ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.

entries.sanskrit: लब्ध-तीर्थो लब्धावसरः स च न बबाधे न प्राहरत् । स मानयन् बभूवेति वाक्य-भेदात् स इत्य् अस्यापौनर् उक्त्यम् ॥४॥
word_for_word: because the sentence is divided at “became”
entries.literal_english: “Labdha-tīrtha” means that he found an opportunity. He did not attack or strike (his opponent while unarmed). Because the sentence is divided at “became,” the later “he” is not redundant; it begins a separate construction, showing that he acted with due regard.

entries.sanskrit: व्यग्रं स-संभ्रमं चक्रं यस्य । विषज्जमानं विशेषेण सङ्गं प्राप्नुवन्तं प्रति । अतद्-विदां तत्-प्रभावम् अजानताम् । आसमन्ताद् आसन् स्म ॥६॥
word_for_word: toward the one approaching to engage closely
of those who did not know that
entries.literal_english: The discus was restless, and its wielder was agitated and confused. The gods were addressing the one who was coming close to engage. Not knowing the Lord’s power, they cried out all around.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.६ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.

entries.sanskrit: स दैत्यस् तम् आत्त-चक्रं निशाम्य दृष्ट्वा अग्रतो व्यवस्थितं च विलोक्य आमर्षेण क्रोधेन परिप्लुतानि क्षुभितानि इन्द्रियाणि यस्य सः । आदशत् दष्टवान् ॥७॥
word_for_word: whose senses were overwhelmed and agitated
entries.literal_english: Seeing the Lord holding the discus and standing before him, the demon’s senses were overwhelmed with indignation and anger. “Ādaśat” means that he bit his lip.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.७ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.
transliteration: sa daityas tam ātta-cakraṃ niśāmya dṛṣṭvā agrato vyavasthitaṃ ca vilokya āmarṣeṇa krodhena pariplutāni kṣubhitāni indriyāṇi yasya saḥ | ādaśat daṣṭavān ||7||

entries.sanskrit: चक्षुर्भ्यां दहन्न् इव सञ्चक्षाणः पश्यन् । इव इति वस्तुतः क्रोधाभावम् आह---हतोऽसि ज्ञातोऽसीति वास्तवोऽर्थः ॥८॥
word_for_word: indicates that in fact there was no anger
this is the intended, actual meaning
entries.literal_english: He gazed as if burning his opponent with his eyes. The word “as if” indicates that the Lord was not actually angry. “You are slain” is intended in the sense “you are found out; I know you.”

entries.literal_english: “Ghaṭasva” means “make an effort; undertake the exertion.” “Kuru” means “do it”—because you wish to conquer.

entries.literal_english: “Hata-māna” describes one whose pride—whose arrogance—has been struck down.

entries.sanskrit: ज्वलन्यो ज्वलनस् तद्वल् लोलुपं ग्रसन-व्यग्रम् । यज्ञाय विष्णुम् आलक्ष्य । अकार्य-करत्वे दृष्टान्तः, विप्रम् उद्दिश्याभिचारं कुर्वन् यथा ॥१३॥
word_for_word: as one performing a harmful rite
entries.literal_english: Blazing like fire and eager to devour, he saw Viṣṇu as the sacrifice. This is an example of acting improperly: like someone who performs an abhichāra rite directed against a brāhmaṇa.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.१३ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.

entries.sanskrit: अन्तः स्वे आकाश-मध्ये चकासत् प्रकाशमानम् । उदीर्ण्आ उत्कटा दीधितिर् दीप्तिर् यस्य। निशात-नेमिना शित-धारेण । हरिर् इन्द्रो यथा तार्क्ष्यस्य पतत्रम् उज्झितं चिच्छेद । देवान् विनिर्जित्य अमृत-कलशं नयता गरुडेन इन्द्र-प्रयुक्त-वज्रस्यामोघस्य मानं दातुं पिच्छम् एकं त्यक्तं तद् यथेन्द्रश् चिच्छेद, छिन्नं च तद् यथा स्वे प्रचकाशे तद्वत् प्रकाशमानम् इत्य् अभिसन्धिः ॥१४॥
word_for_word: in the midst of the sky
by Garuḍa, carrying the pot of nectar
and, once cut, just as it
so too, it is intended to shine radiantly
entries.literal_english: It shone in the middle of the sky, its radiance intense, with a sharply honed rim. The comparison is with Indra cutting a feather left by Garuḍa: after defeating the gods and carrying away the pot of nectar, Garuḍa left one feather in order to honor Indra’s unfailing thunderbolt. Indra cut it, and the severed feather shone in the sky. The intended sense is that this (weapon), too, shone brilliantly.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.१४ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.
transliteration: antaḥ sve ākāśa-madhye cakāsat prakāśamānam | udīrṇā utkaṭā dīdhitir dīptir yasya| niśāta-neminā śita-dhāreṇa | harir indro yathā tārkṣyasya patatram ujjhitaṃ ciccheda | devān vinirjitya amṛta-kalaśaṃ nayatā garuḍena indra-prayukta-vajrasyāmoghasya mānaṃ dātuṃ piccham ekaṃ tyaktaṃ tad yathendraś ciccheda, chinnaṃ ca tad yathā sve pracakāśe tadvat prakāśamānam ity abhisandhiḥ ||14||

entries.sanskrit: अराः सन्त्य् अस्येत्य् अरि चक्रं, तेन बहुधा वृक्णे छिन्ने सति प्रत्य् एत्याभिमुखम् आगत्य हरेर् उरो वक्षः प्रहृत्य ॥१५॥
word_for_word: when he had been cut repeatedly
entries.literal_english: “Ari” means the discus, because it has spokes. After he had been cut repeatedly by it, he returned, came face-to-face with Hari, and struck His chest.

entries.sanskrit: नष्टो भगणो नक्षत्र-समूहो यस्याम् । अनेन दैत्य-बलातिरेकाद् ब्रह्म-दत्त-मुहूर्तातिक्रमो गम्यते । अह्नि नक्षत्राणाम् असंभवात् ॥१९॥
word_for_word: because of the demon’s excessive strength
the passing beyond the moment granted by Brahmā
because the stars are not visible
entries.literal_english: The host of stars had disappeared. This indicates that, owing to the demon’s overwhelming power, the moment allotted by Brahmā had passed, since the stars are not visible in daytime.

entries.literal_english: Female rākṣasas, discharging various weapons, were seen as well.

entries.literal_english: Extremely cruel, violent words—“Cut him! Split him!”—were uttered. The sentence ends here.

entries.sanskrit: प्रादुष्कृतानाम् इति प्रकटिता माया विनाशयत् । "विनाशनम्" इति पाठे यथाश्रुतैव षाष्ठी । त्रीणि सवनानि पादा यस्य । यज्ञ-मूर्तिर् इत्य् अर्थः । त्रयो अस्य पादाः इति श्रुतेः ॥२२॥
word_for_word: the genitive is to be taken just as it stands
“the embodiment of sacrifice” is the meaning
because the śruti says “three are his feet”
entries.literal_english: The illusion that had been manifested was destroyed. In the variant reading “vināśanam,” the genitive is understood directly as written. The three Soma pressings are His feet; hence “Yajña-mūrti” means “the embodiment of sacrifice,” as the śruti says: “Three are his feet.”
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.२२ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.

entries.sanskrit: परितो भ्रमद्-गात्रं शरीरं यस्य । उदस्ते बहिर् निर्गते लोचने यस्य । विशीर्णा बाह्व्-आदयो यस्य । नगेन्द्रो महा-द्रुमः । लुलित उन्मूलितः । नभस्वता वायुना ॥२६॥
word_for_word: whose arms and other limbs were shattered
entries.literal_english: His body rolled about; his eyes protruded, and his arms and other limbs were shattered. “Nagendra” means a great tree, and “lulita” means uprooted—torn out by the wind.

entries.sanskrit: असत आरोपिताल् लिङ्गाल् लिङ्ग-शरीरान् मोक्तुम् इच्छया । वराहस्य पूर्व-पादयोर् एव करत्वात् करेणाहन्न् इति पदा हत इति चाविरुद्धम् ॥२८॥
word_for_word: with the desire to become free
because His forelegs themselves function as hands
entries.literal_english: He desired release from the subtle body superimposed upon the unreal. Since Varāha’s forelegs themselves function as hands, the statements “He struck with His hand” and “He struck with His foot” are not contradictory.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.२८ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.

entries.sanskrit: अखिल-यज्ञानां तन्तवे विस्ताराय कारणायेति वा । अरुन्-तुदो मर्म-भेत्ता ॥३०॥
word_for_word: one who strikes the vulnerable points
entries.literal_english: “Tantu” means the thread or expansion of all sacrifices—or, alternatively, their cause. “Aruntuda” means one who pierces the vital parts.

entries.sanskrit: सादयित्वा हत्वेत्य् अर्थः । पुष्कर-विष्टरादिभिर् ब्रह्मादिभिः संस्तुतः ॥३१॥
word_for_word: by Brahmā, seated on the lotus, and the others
entries.literal_english: “Having brought down” means having killed. He was praised by Brahmā, seated on the lotus, and the other gods.

entries.sanskrit: यथानूक्तं गुरूक्तिम् अनतिक्रम्य मयावादि तव कथितम् । हे सुमित्र ! यथा येन प्रकारेण ॥३२॥
entries.literal_english: I have related it to you as it was told to me, without transgressing my teacher’s words. O good friend, this is how it happened.

entries.sanskrit: भक्ति-मात्रेण पशूनाम् अपि सुलभोऽन्यथा देवानाम् अपि दुर्लभ इति तत् कथा-श्रवणे कस्यानन्दो न स्याद् इत्य् आह---य इति द्वाभ्याम् । झषो ग्राहः । क्रोशन्तीनां सतीनाम् इति कृपालुत्वम् उक्तम् । सङ्कटाद् अचोचयत् ॥३५॥
word_for_word: easily attainable even by animals; otherwise
difficult to attain even for the gods
thus he explains it through the two verses beginning “yaḥ”
entries.literal_english: By devotion alone, [the Lord] is easily attainable even by animals; otherwise, [He is] difficult to attain even for the gods. On hearing that story, who would not feel joy? Thus [it is explained] through the two verses beginning “yaḥ.” “Jhaṣa” means a crocodile or alligator. “Of the virtuous women crying out”—this expresses compassion. He rescued [them] from danger.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.३५ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.

entries.sanskrit: कारणेन पृथिव्य् उद्धरणादिना सूकर-रूपस्य हरेः ॥३७॥
entries.literal_english: This concerns Hari in His boar form, by reason of deeds such as lifting the earth.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.३७ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.

entries.sanskrit: एतद् धरेर् विक्रीडितं शृण्वताम् अन्ते श्री-नारायणो गतिर् भवति । महा-पुण्यं स्वर्गादि-प्रदम् । अलं पवित्रम् अतिशयेन शोधकम् । धन्यं धनावहम् । यशस्यं कीर्ति-करम् । आयुषश् चाशिषां च पदं स्थानं परित्राणं वा प्राणानाम् इन्द्रियाणां च पदम् । अङ्ग हे विदुर ॥३८॥
word_for_word: for those who hear, at the end (of life)
the source of life and blessings
the foundation of the vital breaths and senses
entries.literal_english: Those who hear these playful deeds of Hari attain Śrī Nārāyaṇa as their destination at life’s end. This account is greatly meritorious and bestows heaven and the like; it is exceedingly purifying, brings good fortune and wealth, and bestows fame and renown. It is the source, abode, or protection of life and blessings, and the foundation of the vital breaths and senses. “O dear Vidura.”
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block ३.१९.३८ from pinned Sanskrit source 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179.
transliteration: etad dharer vikrīḍitaṃ śṛṇvatām ante śrī-nārāyaṇo gatir bhavati | mahā-puṇyaṃ svargādi-pradam | alaṃ pavitram atiśayena śodhakam | dhanyaṃ dhanāvaham | yaśasyaṃ kīrti-karam | āyuṣaś cāśiṣāṃ ca padaṃ sthānaṃ paritrāṇaṃ vā prāṇānām indriyāṇāṃ ca padam | aṅga he vidura ||38||
